settings.definition_quote: A general-sum two-player bandit game can be described by a tuple $M=(\mc{A},\mc{B}, r_1, r_2)$ ... The follower observes a (potentially random) reward $r_2(a,b)\in[0,1]$. The leader also observes her own reward $r_1(a,b)\in[0,1]$.

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Follower plays an episodic MDP determined by the leader's action (episodic RL / Markov game).
unmapped: Each leader action determines an episodic MDP with H steps, S states, B actions for the follower
settings.definition_quote: A bandit-RL game is described by the leader's action set $\mc{A}$ (with $|\mc{A}|=A$), and a family of MDPs $M=\set{M^a:a\in\mc{A}}$. Each leader action $a\in\mc{A}$ determines an episodic MDP $M^a$ ... that contains $H$ steps, $S$ states, $B$ actions, with two reward functions $r_1$ and $r_2$.

source.label: theorem:lower-bound-exact-stackelberg
source.quote: For any sample size $n$ and any algorithm for maximizing $\phi_0$ that outputs an action $\what{a}\in\mc{A}$, there exists a bandit game with $A=B=2$ on which the algorithm must suffer from $\Omega(1)$ error with probability at least $1/3$: $\phi_0(\what{a}) \le \max_{a\in\mc{A}} \phi_0(a) - 1/2$.

results.notes: Lower bound on the suboptimality of the output in exact phi_0 (constant 1/2), regardless of sample size; quantity 'other' (suboptimality with probability >= 1/3).

tuning: N = C log(AB/delta)/epsilon^2 queries per pair

source.label: theorem:nested-bandit
source.quote: For any bandit game and $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, Algorithm~\ref{algorithm:bandit} outputs $(\what{a}, \what{b})$ such that with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\phi_0(\what{a}) \ge \phi_{\epsilon/2}(\what{a}) \ge \max_{a\in\mc{A}} \phi_0(a) - \gap_\epsilon - \epsilon$, $\mu_2(\what{a}, \what{b}) \ge \max_{b'\in\mc{B}} \mu_2(\what{a}, b') - \epsilon$ with $n = \wt{O}\paren{ AB/ \epsilon^2}$ samples ... Further, the algorithm runs in $O(n)=\wt{O}(AB/\epsilon^2)$ time.

results.notes: Sample complexity to reach (gap_eps + eps)-approximate Stackelberg with prob >= 1-delta; runtime O(n).

symbols.g: value of gap_eps of the hard instance

conditions: hard instances with Bernoulli rewards and gap_eps = g
failure (error g+eps) with probability at least 1/3

source.label: theorem:lower-bound-nested-bandit
source.quote: There exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that the following holds. For any $\epsilon\in(0,c)$, $g\in[0,c)$, any $A,B\ge 3$, and any algorithm that queries $N\le c\brac{AB/\epsilon^2}$ samples and outputs an estimate $\what{a}\in\mc{A}$, there exists a bandit game $M$ on which $\gap_\epsilon=g$ and the algorithm suffers from $(g+\epsilon)$ error ... with probability at least $1/3$.

results.notes: Proof gives explicit N <= AB/(864 eps^2).

symbols.n_states: number of states S of the follower MDP

source.label: theorem:two-level-rl
source.quote: For any bandit-RL game and sufficiently small $\epsilon\le O(1/H^2S^2)$, Algorithm~\ref{algorithm:two-level-rl} with $n=\wt{O}(H^5S^2AB/\epsilon^2+H^7S^4AB/\epsilon)$ episodes of play can return $(\what{a}, \what{\pi}^b)$ such that with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\phi_0(\what{a}) \ge \phi_{\epsilon/2}(\what{a}) \ge \max_{a\in\mc{A}} \phi_0(a) - \gap_\epsilon - \epsilon$ ... Further, the algorithm runs in ${\rm poly}(HSAB/\delta\epsilon)$ time.

results.notes: Counted in episodes; log(HSAB/delta eps) factors hidden.

tuning: N = O(d log(d/delta)/eps^2) queries per core-set point

source.label: theorem:linear-bandit
source.quote: For any linear bandit game, Algorithm~\ref{algorithm:linear-bandit} outputs a $(\gap_\eps+\eps)$-approximate Stackelberg equilibrium $(\what{a}, \what{b})$ with probability at least $1-\delta$: $\phi_0(\what{a}) \ge \phi_{\eps/2}(\what{a}) \ge \max_{a\in\mc{A}} \phi_0(a) - \gap_{\eps} - \eps$, in at most $n=\wt{O}(d^2/\eps^2)$ queries.

results.notes: Paper states runtime poly(A,B,d,1/eps^2) in subsequent text.

symbols.g: value of gap_eps of the hard instance

conditions: hard instance uses standard-basis features (tabular bandit game embedded in R^d), Bernoulli rewards
failure with probability at least 1/3 (inherited from Theorem 3)

source.label: theorem:lower-bound-linear-bandit
source.quote: There exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that the following holds. For any $\eps\in(0,c)$, $g\in[0,c)$, and any algorithm that queries $n\le c[d/\eps^2]$ samples and outputs an estimate $\what{a}\in\mc{A}$, there exists a linear bandit game $M$ with feature dimension $d$, on which $\gap_\eps=g$ and the algorithm suffers from $(g+\eps)$ error

results.notes: Probability level not stated in the theorem itself; derived from Theorem 3 (prob >= 1/3). Bernoulli rewards are not 1-sub-Gaussian-noise exactly but bounded.

tuning: N = C log(AB/delta)/epsilon^2 queries per pair
